Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11

Duration: 48 minutes
Hosted by: Avery Chen (Redwood AE)

Summary (auto):
Quick procurement intake to surface approval criteria, legal redline process for MSA/DPA, and pricing guardrails for pilot. Customer is healthcare vertical; strong data residency and audit requirements. Plan: send docs, run benchmark, reconvene procurement review.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redline expectations
- SLA levels and remediation language
- Pricing paths: hosted pay-as-you-go vs reserved/dedicated commit
- Security evidence: SOC2, pen test, KMS integrations
- Onboarding timeline and procurement gating

Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, um so thanks for taking the time today. I'm Avery from Redwood, and with me is Miguel, our solutions eng. Quick sound check?
[00:08] Jordan (Clarity Procurement): Yep, we can hear you. Thanks for doing this, we want to move fast but also make sure legal + security are happy.
[00:14] Miguel (Redwood SE): Hey all, Miguel here. I'll cover perf and the dedicated/reserved tradeoffs when we get there.
[00:20] Amrita (Clarity Legal): Thanks. I'll jump in on the DPA/MSA questions — we have a few non-standard clauses we need to surface.
[00:26] Samir (InfoSec): And I'm Samir, InfoSec. We'll want KM S integration details and audit logs, retention, you know the usual.
[00:33] Avery: Great. To kick off, Jordan, can you summarize the procurement thresholds and what approvers you need to get to? like dollar bands and who signs?
[00:40] Jordan: Sure. For anything under $50k we can sign on a standard PO; above that it goes to sourcing and legal. For anything over $200k it routes to the exec procurement board. Our ideal pilot is in the $25-75k window so, um we're hoping to keep it under the big gate.
[01:02] Avery: Good, that's helpful. On our side we usually propose a 90-day pilot with hosted credits, then if you want reserved capacity / dedicated we'll provide a term sheet. The key thing legal asks about is indemnity and data handling in the DPA.
[01:18] Amrita: Right — the DPA exceptions we'll likely ask: deletion SLA guarantees, subprocessors list, and KMS/HSM assurances. Also can you confirm whether logs contain PHI pseudonymization? This is health data so that's a hard requirement.
[01:32] Miguel: Quick clarification — when you say "PHI", are you planning to send raw PHI into the model or will it be pseudonymized at ingestion? The host pattern matters for our recommended deployment.
[01:40] Tanya (VP Product): We'll likely send identifiable records during the pilot for end-to-end validation, but only on a scoped dataset and with contractual protections.
[01:49] Samir: That increases our need for VPC/private deployment options. We want to avoid egress to shared tenants.
[01:55] Avery: Understood. We have Private (VPC) and on-prem options; Private keeps the runtime in your VPC with customer-managed keys for storage and optional bring-your-own-key into the cluster. Miguel: do you want to add detail on KMS/HSM?
[02:06] Miguel: Yeah — so we support customer-managed KMS integration, and we can integrate with common HSM flows for key wrapping. Note: some of our docs call it "Redwood Consoel" in older exports, so please ignore that typos in the packet. Also, our KV cache is sometimes transcribed as KV cash in older reports, ha.
[02:24] Amrita: Thanks, those are the things our legal folks look for. For the DPA language we typically request notification windows for breaches, and a clause about audit rights — do you provide SOC2 and pen-test reports?
[02:35] Avery: Yes, we can provide SOC2 Type II, most recent pen test summary, and a VPS-like report for the Private deployment. We'll share redacted reports and a whitepaper link.
[02:44] Jordan: On the commercial side — we need both sticker price and a pricing path for a committed Dedicated pool if we like results. How do you usually structure pricing approvals?
[02:52] Avery: There's a couple of common paths: hosted pay-as-you-go with token-based billing, or reserved capacity (monthly commit) which gets a discount. For enterprise we do committed units with guaranteed throughput and an SLA. Miguel, maybe run through perf/cost tradeoffs?
[03:06] Miguel: Sure — rough numbers: for conversational workloads with ~2.5k context, hosted will have variable unit cost; reserved GPUs reduce cost per token by roughly 30-45% depending on utilization. We typically present a cost model spreadsheet — we'll attach that. For healthcare workloads where latency matters, dedicated pools with autoscaling but pinned nodes deliver consistent p99.
[03:28] Samir: What about SLOs and credits? Our procurement requires SLOs in the MSA — e.g., availability and credits for downtime.
[03:36] Avery: We offer SLA-backed uptime targets for Dedicated customers — standard is 99.9 for dedicated, hosted is best-effort but we can offer enhanced tiers. Credits are tiered by severity; legal can request precise SLA text and handoff matrix.
[03:49] Amrita: On indemnity, we need to see the MSA's carve-outs for third-party content and limitations on consequential damages. Also, for PHI there's a request to add specific breach notification windows (48 hours) — is that negotiable?
[04:03] Avery: We'll surface our standard MSA but note major legal asks up front. Some customers get 48-hour notification for critical incidents via enterprise SLAs; others accept 72 hours. We'll mark this as an exception to track.
[04:12] Jordan: Procurement also needs clarity on billing cadence and PO vs invoice paths. For pilots we prefer net-30 invoices tied to a PO; for committed services we use net-45 with milestone invoices.
[04:25] Avery: Noted. We'll flag billing options in the commercial worksheet.
[04:29] Miguel: Two practical items on the tech side — we'll need a contact for a proof-of-concept VPN/VPC setup and a test dataset for performance runs. Who owns that?
[04:38] Jordan: I can own the procurement paperwork, but for the network setup it'll be Samir and our cloud infra team. I'll introduce them after this call.
[04:47] Samir: Sounds good. Also, we need to review retention settings — logs must be kept for at least 12 months and access to logs must be auditable via RBAC.
[04:56] Miguel: We can configure retention and RBAC roles; our console (sorry, Consoel in some docs) supports per-token traceability and tracing hooks. We can share a screenshot in the security packet.
[05:06] Amrita: Are you able to accept any specific data residency requirements? E.g., all processing in us-east-1 due to patient data residency?
[05:14] Avery: Yes, we have region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated; Private gives you full control. For hosted, we can limit model routing to a region but it's not a full VPC separation unless you choose Private.
[05:25] Jordan: On the legal flow, what's your redline cadence? How long do we expect negotiation to take once we hand over the MSA/DPA?
[05:33] Avery: For standard customers it's usually 2-4 weeks for minor redlines. For enterprise with exceptions it can go 4-8 weeks depending on the number of DPA exceptions — given you're in healthcare, plan for the longer end unless we limit exceptions.
[05:44] Amrita: We'll try to bundle major exceptions together to accelerate review. One ask: can you provide a response matrix that maps each DPA clause to Redwood's stance and alternative language? It helps legal triage.
[05:55] Avery: Yes, we can provide a clause-by-clause response. We'll include a table: clause, standard language, customer-proposed language, redwood stance.
[06:03] Miguel: On benchmarking — we'll run a 1-hour perf test with representative payloads. Expect a spreadsheet with p50/p90/p99 latencies, token cost, and GPU utilization. That helps justify reserved capacity economics.
[06:15] Jordan: Good. Contractually, procurement needs an internal approval packet — would you provide an executive summary and cost delta options?
[06:22] Avery: We'll prepare a 1-page exec summary + 2 pricing scenarios: conservative hosted pilot and reserved commit POC with discounts.
[06:30] Tanya: If legal insists on added audit rights, are you open to on-site audits or remote audit packs?
[06:36] Miguel: We generally support remote audit evidence and SOC2 reports. On-site audits are rare but possible under Private deployments and with appropriate NDA/controls; they'd be scoped.
[06:46] Amrita: Ok noted. Another flag — subprocessors list. We need to know third-party infra providers and whether any training data is persisted.
[06:54] Avery: We'll share an up-to-date subprocessors list. For model-hosted services we don't retain training data from customer prompts; we do have transient KV caching for the session unless you disable it. We'll clarify the retention policy in the DPA.
[07:07] Samir: The transient cache is fine if it's ephemeral and not written to persistent storage; we want to see deletion timelines.
[07:13] Miguel: We'll include cache TTLs and persistence behavior. Note, some technical docs use 'KV cache' but older transcripts mung that to 'KV cash', so sorry for the noise.
[07:23] Jordan: Timeline wise — if we get the MSA/DPA today and redlines early next week, can we target a procurement sign-off by end of month?
[07:31] Avery: Potentially. If you can limit DPA exceptions to a small set and get signoff from legal quickly, procurement can often process the PO within 10 business days. We'll need the PO approver list from you.
[07:40] Jordan: I'll send approver list and thresholds (action item).
[07:44] Amrita: One more question on SLA credits — do you tie credits to service window per region or per deployment?
[07:51] Avery: Credits are applied per deployment; Dedicated gets strongest guarantees. We'll attach sample SLA language so you can review.
[07:59] Miguel: To close, we'll also include a security packet link: SOC2, pentest high-level, subprocessors, KMS integration guide, and a short architecture diagram for Private deploy.
[08:10] Tanya: Perfect. From product side we'll need to validate edge cases around content filtering and model hallucinations — is there a remediation plan that will be contractually acceptable?
[08:21] Avery: We'll include our default content policy and a catalog of mitigations — e.g., model selection, prompt engineering, reranking, and human-in-loop fallback. Those can be appended to an SOW if needed.
[08:34] Amrita: Ok — can you also confirm data deletion guarantees post-contract termination? That's a standard clause we will gate on.
[08:42] Avery: We'll include data deletion timelines and certificate of deletion for Private and Dedicated. Hosted has documented retention windows.
[08:50] Jordan: That's helpful. Let's recap next steps.
[08:54] Avery: Recap: (1) we'll send templated MSA/DPA and clause-by-clause response; (2) Miguel will run benchmark and share perf/cost workbook; (3) Avery will send pricing worksheet with hosted vs reserved scenarios and SLA samples; (4) Jordan will send approver list and Samir will loop in infra.
[09:12] Amrita: And we will return DPA redlines and any required legal language by 2/17.
[09:17] Avery: Great. Any final questions?
[09:20] Samir: None from me. Thanks, everyone.
[09:23] Avery: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email and schedule the procurement-only review for 2026-02-17 per Jordan's availability.
[09:30] Call ends with polite sign-offs and brief chit-chat (off transcript).
